why_relevant: Creditas was reported as one of the CZ record-holders for connected third parties; a smaller, faster-moving bank whose open-banking page is a useful leading indicator of API practice shifts.
Private/investment bank TPP portal; broadens coverage beyond the retail majors and shows how non-retail institutions schedule PSD2 interface changes.
Document-based (rather than portal-based) publication of TPP access rules — a different publication pattern worth capturing because change notices land as dated PDFs rather than changelog entries.

source_name: Fio banka – API bankovnictví / obchodní podmínky
source_subtype: bank API page + T&C PDF series
why_relevant: Fio runs a long-standing proprietary API alongside PSD2 duties and publishes its OP as dated PDFs (e.g. OP_FB.pdf, RSI_OP_240201.pdf where the filename encodes the effective date) — a machine-friendly effective-date signal.

source_name: GoPay – Ceník a obchodní podmínky (dated T&C series)
why_relevant: Non-bank payment institution (supervised by ČNB and NBB) publishing versioned T&C with explicit 'účinnost <date>' in the page title/slug. Gives the PSP-side (rather than bank-side) arrival date of payments-law and scheme-rule changes.

source_name: Comgate Payments – nápověda / povolené služby a podmínky
why_relevant: Licensed CZ payment institution under ČNB supervision; its help/T&C pages document permitted merchant segments and card-scheme/regulatory constraints, effectively surfacing Visa/Mastercard and ČNB rule changes as operational merchant-facing rules.

source_name: Citfin – Oznámení o změně Všeobecných obchodních podmínek (news-style change notices)
why_relevant: Example of a smaller CZ payment institution publishing 'Oznámení o změně VOP' as a dated news item — the canonical phrasing to fingerprint across the whole PSP population when building an automated notice detector.
Small-bank open-banking page; needed for population completeness — smaller banks often publish PSD2 interface availability/derogation statements that larger banks bury.

source_name: PixelBrothers – blog on ČSOB legacy API endpoint shutdown (integrator commentary)
why_relevant: Integrator-side commentary that surfaces and dates bank API deprecations faster and more legibly than the bank portals themselves; useful as a tripwire that a bank has published a deadline, then verify against the bank source.

Referenced by the cz-banking-psd2 repo as the more current index of CZ bank APIs (a CzechCrunch piece cites ~28 connectable banks via such a portal). Potentially the best-maintained aggregator for this cell, but not confirmed in this run.

source_name: Měšec.cz — consumer finance & banking regulation desk
why_relevant: Long-running Czech consumer-finance daily (Internet Info group) that tracks what changes for bank clients when payment/banking rules take effect; explains ČNB and MF ČR measures in operational terms and flags de-facto compliance deadlines. Also hosts a full-text law library (zakony/zakon-o-platebnim-styku) useful for versioned legal text.

Major Czech personal-finance portal covering bank fees, payment rules and regulatory changes affecting retail clients; strong on 'what changes from January' framing that surfaces effective dates and transition periods.

The Czech banking trade magazine (originally 'Hlas banky', ČNB-published until 1998, then Economia, since 2013 4H Production). Its dedicated 'Regulace' rubric carries practitioner and compliance-officer commentary on upcoming CRR/CRD, DORA, PSD3, AML rules and ČNB supervisory expectations — the closest thing to an industry-insider read on Czech banking regulation.

Czech internet/technology daily; covers the digital side of financial regulation — eIDAS/BankID, instant payments infrastructure, digital identity, data and cyber rules (NIS2/DORA) as they hit banks and payment providers. Complements finance desks that skip the technical layer.

The Czech business daily of record (Economia, est. 1990). Best single source for contested legislation, lobbying by ČBA/banks, MF ČR drafts and interviews with ČNB board members; frequently the first to report supervisory pressure and enforcement before official publication.
Dedicated banking/finance rubric of the E15 economic daily; a mostly-open alternative to paywalled HN for tracking bank levies, ČNB decisions, licensing and payment-market disputes.

Largest-reach Czech online news outlet with an investigative economics desk; covers bank fees, consumer-protection enforcement, and political fights over financial legislation with mass audience impact — the coverage that actually moves Czech policy timing.

Public-service broadcaster news site with investigative unit; reliable, non-paywalled reporting on ČNB decisions, financial fraud, enforcement and legislative process. Public-service status makes it a good credibility anchor when private media disagree.

SME/business-practice portal (Internet Info) that reports how payment and banking rules land on merchants and firms — e.g. gaps in the Payment Services Act for corporates and public bodies. Valuable for merchant/acquiring-side regulatory impact that consumer desks miss.

Boutique Czech financial-regulation law firm publishing on ČNB licensing under PSD2, e-money, crypto and fintech supervision; practitioners (e.g. Jan Šovar) are recurring media commentators, so the blog often previews criticism of drafts before mainstream coverage.

Czech fintech online magazine running since 2016, with long-form interviews with regulators' counterparties and licensing lawyers; captures industry pushback on ČNB supervisory tightening that formal channels do not record.

Startup/business outlet with strong fintech coverage and opinion columns on where regulation is pushing the Czech fintech market (BNPL, consolidation, licensing burden). Useful for early signals on market exits caused by regulatory cost.

Finance/economics outlet tied to the Roklen group; publishes practitioner interviews on why fintechs collide with Czech and EU regulation and on EU market integration — a source of critique-of-regulation framing.

Market newswire (KBC/ČSOB-affiliated) with a timestamped hot-news archive; fastest Czech-language relay of ČNB board decisions, capital requirements and EU regulatory news, with a browsable archive good for backfilling timelines.

Free consolidated ('úplné znění') texts of Czech financial statutes including Act No. 370/2017 Coll. on Payments; useful for pinning which version of a rule a media story is describing and for detecting amendments.

Industry body whose positions and press statements are the raw material for the critical media coverage in this cell; a pointer to member firms, spokespeople and consultation responses on Czech/EU payment regulation.
